Q: Removing Conda environment A:

After making sure your environment is not active, type:

conda remove --name ENVIRONMENT --all

Q: How to simulate ThisPresentation in PowerPoint VBA A:

I believe I have come up with a better solution than anything I've seen elsewhere, so let me share it here. It doesn't require making any assumption or any adaptation for each specific project, it works all the time, in all cases.

The idea is to use a beacon in the Presentation that can only be lit by that very Presentation, not even by a copy containing the same code.

It uses On Error, but you can narrow the screening based on other criteria like file names, properties or add-in names if you don't like that (I do use a pre-filter in my version, so I don't hit the On Error in general), but that makes it project-specific and it's not necessary.

In a standard module that we will call The_Lighthouse, have the Beacon as a Public Boolean variable and a Sub to light it:

Public Beacon As Boolean

Public Sub light_beacon()
    Beacon = True
End Sub

Then anywhere in the project (but it makes sense to have that in the same module), we can use the following to simulate ThisPresentation – this won't work for add-ins, but I'll come back to that after:

Function ThisPresentation() As Presentation

    Dim pr As Presentation
    Dim macroName As String

    'Make sure the beacon is off
    Beacon = False

    For Each pr In Application.Presentations
        macroName = "'" & pr.FullName & "'!The_Lighthouse.light_beacon"

        On Error Resume Next
        Application.Run macroName
        On Error GoTo 0

        If Beacon = True Then
            Set ThisPresentation = pr
            Exit Function
        End If
    Next pr
    
End Function

Only ThisPresentation can light its own Beacon, so you are 100% sure to get the Presentation that is running the code and that's what we want.

Now the version for add-ins:

Function ThisAddin() As AddIn

    Dim ai As AddIn
    Dim macroName As String

    'Make sure the beacon is off
    Beacon = False

    For Each ai In Application.AddIns
        If ai.Loaded Then
            macroName = "'" & ai.FullName & "'!The_Lighthouse.light_beacon"

            On Error Resume Next
            Application.Run macroName
            On Error GoTo 0

            If Beacon = True Then
                Set ThisAddin = ai
                Exit Function
            End If
        End If
    Next ai

End Function

Exact same approach, and you can call Subs in add-ins using Application.Run macroName, that does work.

And now a combination of the two if you need something universal:

Function ThisObject() As Object

    Dim pr As Presentation
    Dim ai As AddIn
    Dim macroName As String

    'Make sure the beacon is off
    Beacon = False

    'Screen the open presentations
    For Each pr In Application.Presentations
        macroName = "'" & pr.FullName & "'!The_Lighthouse.light_beacon"

        On Error Resume Next
        Application.Run macroName
        On Error GoTo 0

        If Beacon = True Then
            Set ThisObject = pr
            Exit Function
        End If
    Next pr

    'If that was not a presentation, then screen the loaded add-ins
    For Each ai In Application.AddIns
        If ai.Loaded Then
            macroName = "'" & ai.FullName & "'!The_Lighthouse.light_beacon"

            On Error Resume Next
            Application.Run macroName
            On Error GoTo 0

            If Beacon = True Then
                Set ThisObject = ai
                Exit Function
            End If
        End If
    Next ai

End Function

And that's it, you have the ultimate (?) ThisPresentation!

Q: How do I break a string in YAML over multiple lines? A:

1. Block notation (plain, flow-style, scalar): Newlines become spaces and extra newlines after the block are removed

---
# Note: It has one new line after the string
content:
    Arbitrary free text
    over multiple lines stopping
    after indentation changes...

...

Equivalent JSON

{
 "content": "Arbitrary free text over multiple lines stopping after indentation changes..."
}

2. Literal block scalar: A literal block scalar | will include the newlines and any trailing spaces. But it removes extra newlines after the block.

---
# After string we have two spaces and two new lines
content1: |
 Arbitrary free text
 over "multiple lines" stopping
 after indentation changes...


...

Equivalent JSON

{
 "content1": "Arbitrary free text\nover \"multiple lines\" stopping\nafter indentation changes...  \n"
}

3. + indicator with literal block scalar: keep extra newlines after block

---
# After string we have two new lines
plain: |+
 This unquoted scalar
 spans many lines.


...

Equivalent JSON

{
 "plain": "This unquoted scalar\nspans many lines.\n\n\n"
}

4. – indicator with literal block scalar: – means that the newline at the end of the string is removed.

---
# After the string, we have two new lines
plain: |-
 This unquoted scalar
 spans many lines.


...

Equivalent JSON

{
 "plain": "This unquoted scalar\nspans many lines."
}

5. Folded block scalar (>):

will fold newlines to spaces and, but removes extra newlines after the block.

---
folded_newlines: >
 this is really a
 single line of text
 despite appearances


...

Equivalent JSON

{
 "fold_newlines": "this is really a single line of text despite appearances\n"
}

Q: VBA and Pivot Tables: getting two data fields A:

I made some revisions to your code so try this:

Sub CreatePivot()
' Create the 5 summary pivot tables using the TRADE_LIST sheet as data
Dim LastRow, LastCol As Long
Dim dataSource, destination As String
Dim wb As Workbook
Dim data_sheet, pivot1 As Worksheet

Set wb = ThisWorkbook
Set data_sheet = wb.Sheets("DATA") 'in your code, you forgot to include WB
Set pivot1 = wb.Sheets("PIVOT")

' (1) Source data from the TRADE_LIST sheet and create a pivot cache from source data _
  to use for each pivot table

'i changed this part to cover all data 
LastRow = data_sheet.Cells(data_sheet.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row
LastCol = data_sheet.Cells(1, data_sheet.Columns.Count).End(xlToLeft).Column

'PivotCache creation requires arguments in string format, no need to use Set
dataSource = data_sheet.Name & "!" & data_sheet.Cells(1, 1).Resize(LastRow, LastCol).Address(ReferenceStyle:=xlR1C1)
destination = pivot1.Name & "!" & pivot1.Range("A1").Address(ReferenceStyle:=xlR1C1)

'here we use the datasource and destination
wb.PivotCaches.Create(SourceType:=xlDatabase, SourceData:= _
    dataSource, Version:=xlPivotTableVersion12).CreatePivotTable _
    TableDestination:=destination, TableName:="PivotTable1", DefaultVersion _
    :=xlPivotTableVersion12

'after creating pivot, add the Row Field
With pivot1.PivotTables("PivotTable1").PivotFields("Comment")
    .Orientation = xlRowField
    .Position = 1
End With

'then add the column fields
With pivot1
    .PivotTables("PivotTable1").AddDataField .PivotTables( _
        "PivotTable1").PivotFields("NOM"), "Sum of NOM", xlSum
    .PivotTables("PivotTable1").AddDataField .PivotTables( _
        "PivotTable1").PivotFields("NOM_MOVE"), "Sum of NOM_MOVE", xlSum
End With

End Sub

Hope this get's you started.

Q: How to do onclick event in VBA/VBScript A:

Here's what you're looking for:

document.getElementById("tabnew").attachEvent "onclick",getref("onclick")

First argument is the event ("onclick","onmouseover"... See: http://www.tutorialspoint.com/vbscript/vbscript_events.htm (very bottom of page for list of events)) Second argument is a getref of the name of your sub.

Q: How to empty or clear heap memory dynamically A:

Increase the heap space.. and turn on auto delete, like in eclipse if you go to preferences and manage the heap space; you can click the trash button there
